analysis.title: US Watch: October FOMC review: Window dressing
key_insights: The FOMC held rates at its October meeting. The statement suggests the Fed wants to move slowly, likely at a quarterly pace, because it is unsure how restrictive policy is.

The statement upgraded the growth descriptor from "solid" to "strong", which BofA calls hawkish on the margin. The inflation language, that more information will help determine the appropriate stance, signals low conviction on where the neutral rate is but is consistent with another hike in December.

Two dissents came from Cook and Hammack. Cook's dissent was a surprise because BofA saw her as close to the committee median. Logan did not dissent, which also surprised BofA given her earlier comments that more hikes were needed.

In the press conference Chair Warsh leaned on tighter financial conditions as evidence that the September hike is working. He declined to guide on a December hike. BofA calls the presser dovish and lacking clarity, and says Warsh risks losing relevance if he neither guides nor surprises markets.

BofA still expects two more hikes but now on a quarterly cadence, in December 2026 and March 2027. The terminal rate forecast stays at 4.25-4.5%, held through end-2027, with no material change to its macro forecasts.

Risks to the call are two-sided. The bigger risk is that the Fed falls behind the curve, with 25-50bp of extra hikes possible in 2027. Alternatively, favorable base effects could pull y/y core inflation down enough for the Fed to stop after the December 2026 hike.

The Treasury curve twist steepened after the FOMC. From the start of the press conference the 2Y yield fell 6bps and the 30Y rose 4bps. BofA reads this as the bond market doubting Warsh's credibility on inflation. The 2Y decline was led by real rates, and the 30Y rise by higher real rates plus wider breakevens.
BofA keeps its view for higher front-end rates and a flatter curve over time, and says the long end will keep pressuring the Fed until it is more serious about inflation.
Higher long-end yields raise the risk that Treasury cuts long-end auction sizes, possibly at the November 4 refunding, after the August increase in long-end buyback sizes.

The USD fell about 0.2-0.3% during the FOMC, mostly during the press conference. The move was roughly half the ~-0.5% drop after the July press conference. Markets still price about 21bp of December hikes, down from 23bp before the meeting.

Warsh said the Fed will devote one of its eight 2027 meetings (in the fall) to long-term strategy rather than rates, and from 2028 will hold two such meetings and only six policy decisions. BofA says FX read this as an incrementally dovish signal.

trade_ideas.rationale: A Fed slow to respond to strong activity and elevated inflation raises the risk of larger future hikes.
trade_ideas.risk: The path will not be a straight line, and favorable base effects could lead the Fed to stop after one more hike.

tension_points.bull_case: Caution is vindicated if favorable base effects pull y/y core inflation down next year, and the Fed could stop after one more hike in December 2026.
tension_points.bear_case: By moving slower the Fed falls behind the curve, financial conditions ease or tighten perversely as credibility is questioned, and 25-50bp of extra hikes could follow in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Y/y core inflation rolling off significantly in 2027 due to base effects would validate the slower path. Long-end yields continuing to rise would point to more hikes.
